subject: Request: C-suite approval for extended POC & credits for AtlasWare
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kaplan <sara@atlasware.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: C-suite approval for extended POC & credits for AtlasWare

Team —

Quick escalation: AtlasWare (mid-market SI, potential ARR $380k first 12 months) is stuck in procurement and needs more time on the POC to complete their integration and SI partner validation. They’ve hit our standard PLG cap (30k credit / 2 week trial) and are asking for: a 6-week extension on the POC plus an additional $12k in free credits to cover expanded integration testing and embedding reruns.

Why this matters:
- Signal: AtlasWare has already integrated our SDK and completed two successful end-to-end demos with the product team.
- Traction: Their usage shows increasing token consumption (see attached usage snapshot) and a clear path to production (embedding-based search + summarization).
- Sales case: We estimate a 12–18 month conversion to $380k ARR with a 60% probability if the extended POC proves stable.

Ask: C-suite approval for a one-time exception: 6-week extension + $12k credits (equivalent to ~400k generation tokens at our blended rates). Alternate, if you prefer more conservative exposure: approve a 4-week extension + $10k credits.

Risks/mitigations:
- Cost risk: ~12k exposure up-front. Offset by requiring AtlasWare to sign a short SOW addendum with a commitment to a technical review and procurement timeline.
- Abuse risk: We’ll add usage caps and logging, export all telemetry to their SRE.

I’ve included a draft SOW and the usage snapshot for your review. If we approve, I’ll route to Legal/Finance for the addendum and have DealOps record the concession in Salesforce/HubSpot.

Recommendation (what I’d sign off on): Approve the 4-week + $10k option unless Rishi wants to stretch to 6 weeks based on the ARR probability.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Atlasware_POC_usage_snapshot.csv, Atlasware_SOW_draft.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Kaplan <sara@atlasware.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: C-suite approval for extended POC & credits for AtlasWare

Monica — thanks for the write-up, looks sensible. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I sign off:
1) Can you confirm the deal close target if POC goes well (calendar month)?
2) What is the expected incremental cost to us if we do the 6-week ask vs the 4-week ask (rough $/token estimate)?

From what I can see, the upside is solid, but I want a clear escalation path if procurement stalls further. Also please attach the usage snapshot you referenced (I don’t see it in my client).

On the second point — if we agree to 6 weeks we should require a procurement commit milestone (e.g., signed LoI or POC acceptance criteria) before the last disbursement of credits.

- Sean
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Sean — attaching the snapshot and a brief cost delta table below. Also added the proposed SOW addendum language to require procurement milestones.

Attachment: Atlasware_POC_usage_snapshot.csv; Atlasware_SOW_draft.pdf

Cost delta (very conservative estimate):
- 4-week extension + $10k credits ≈ additional $10k exposure (we consider this fixed credit)
- 6-week extension + $12k credits ≈ additional $12k exposure
- Marginal infra impact: negligible given caching and current usage pattern; primary cost is credits we’ll absorb.

Procurement milestone we’ll require (SOW addendum):
- AtlasWare to provide a signed Letter of Intent or procurement schedule within 3 weeks of extension start.
- If LOI not provided by then, remaining credits are paused.

Why I prefer the 6-week ask: their integration is with an external SI partner and the partner’s timeline was the gating factor; 4 weeks may not be enough to validate edge-case data flows. However I’ll accept the 4-week + $10k option if leadership wants to minimize exposure.

If approved, I’ll create the HubSpot concession record (HubSpot deal link below) and route the addendum to Legal.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5723
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_Atlasware-POC

Thanks,
Monica

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: C-suite approval for extended POC & credits for AtlasWare

Appreciate the concise summary and the attach. I’ll approve a one-time exception with these conditions:
1) Approve: 4-week extension + $10,000 in free credits (one-time).
2) Condition: Credits paid in two tranches — 50% on extension start, 50% on receipt of signed LOI or procurement schedule (as defined in the SOW addendum). If LOI is not provided within 3 weeks, remaining credits are void.
3) Legal to sign the SOW addendum and Finance to record the concession in the Deal Desk register (Deal ID HW-5723).
4) Product to enable a hard usage cap and export of telemetry to AtlasWare SRE for the extension period.

Monica — please execute the above, loop in Legal/Finance, and confirm when the concession is recorded in HubSpot/Deal Desk. CC me on the final addendum.

— Rishi
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
